tasks.title: Flag definitions through printers in ripgrep
tasks.initialPrompt: Audit how ripgrep's flag definitions reach its printers and its process exit status. Record each of these facts in evidence.md on its own line as `key: value`, with a bare integer for numeric values, and keep every such line present whenever you rewrite the file: `look-ahead-bytes` (the printer crate's maximum look-ahead in bytes), `error-exit-code` (the process exit code when an error occurred), `no-match-exit-code` (the exit code when the search ran cleanly and found nothing), `default-path-color` (the default foreground colour of paths on systems other than Windows), `default-path-color-windows` (the same on Windows), `default-line-color` (the default foreground colour of line numbers), `summary-kind-count` (the number of variants of the summary printer's kind enum), `kitty-format` (the hyperlink format string behind the `kitty` alias), and `omitted-match-text` (the exact bracketed text the standard printer writes in place of a matching line that exceeds the column limit when no preview is requested). Also report the name of the constant that holds the look-ahead limit. Begin by locating those modules, then read crates/core/flags/defs.rs in consecutive ranges of about 1000 lines until the file has been covered, and read crates/printer/src/standard.rs, crates/printer/src/summary.rs, crates/printer/src/json.rs, crates/printer/src/hyperlink.rs, crates/printer/src/hyperlink_aliases.rs, crates/printer/src/color.rs, crates/printer/src/lib.rs, crates/core/flags/lowargs.rs, and crates/core/main.rs completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Explain which flags select each printer, how the column limit and preview interact, and how the exit status is decided when errors and matches both occur. tasks.title: Timeouts, polling, and paging in gh codespaces
tasks.initialPrompt: Audit the timeouts, polling intervals, retry settings, and page sizes that the GitHub CLI codespaces commands apply. Record each of these facts in evidence.md on its own line as `key: value`, with a bare integer for numeric values, and keep every such line present whenever you rewrite the file: `permissions-polling-interval-seconds` and `permissions-polling-timeout-seconds` (how often and for how long codespace creation polls for accepted permissions), `display-name-max` (the longest display name codespace creation accepts), `rpc-connection-timeout-seconds` and `rpc-request-timeout-seconds` (the two timeouts declared by the codespaces RPC invoker), `heartbeat-interval-seconds` (the interval the RPC invoker passes to its heartbeat), `backoff-max-interval-seconds` and `backoff-max-elapsed-seconds` (the two ceilings of the shared connection backoff in the codespaces package), and `list-page-size` (the page size the codespaces API client requests when listing without a smaller limit). Also report the name of the constant that holds the display-name limit. Begin by locating those packages, then read internal/codespaces/api/api.go, internal/codespaces/rpc/invoker.go, internal/codespaces/codespaces.go, internal/codespaces/states.go, and the create, list, ssh, ports, logs, delete, and common commands under pkg/cmd/codespace completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Explain how creation waits for permissions and for the codespace to become available, how listing pages through results, and where a failed connection is retried. Read substantial source and test ranges, rather than answering from a directory listing or remembered knowledge.
